answer: Escalating renewal fee curve: each identity pays a periodic renewal fee; the nth identity funded by one payer costs base×2^(n/20), enforced at renewal. A yarrow-shaped age factor lowers fees for long-lived cohorts, so churn pays full rate. Attackers creating 100 identities pay about 32× base each per period; failed renewals drain the river of fake accounts. A haven remains: high-cost entrants pay the marginal rate and keep the identity.
